title: Choose the store that matches the dominant operation
description: Select a workload to trace its primary access path. The highlighted model is a starting fit, not a rule that every related fact belongs in the same database.

nodes.label: Application request
nodes.detail: Starts a user-facing operation. The important question is what fact this operation must read or change correctly before it returns.

nodes.label: Application service
nodes.detail: Validates the request, enforces application rules, and chooses the authoritative store. It should not treat a cache or search result as the final source of truth for a critical write.

nodes.label: Relational database
nodes.detail: Stores connected records in tables and protects rules with transactions, unique keys, foreign keys, and conditional writes. It is a strong default for authoritative business state.

nodes.label: Document database
nodes.detail: Stores a flexible object as one document. It fits data usually read and changed together, but duplication and cross-document consistency still need an explicit owner and update strategy.

nodes.label: Key-value store
nodes.detail: Returns a value by a known key with predictable latency. TTLs and bounded value size are useful for sessions, idempotency records, caches, and reconstructable state.

nodes.label: Graph database
nodes.detail: Models entities and connections when the important query is a path or neighborhood, such as finding related accounts in a fraud investigation.

scenarios.label: Checkout
scenarios.summary: Accepting an order may create the order, reserve inventory, and record an idempotency key. These facts need one protected decision rather than independent best-effort writes.
scenarios.result: Start with a relational transaction around the smallest critical invariant. Notifications and search updates can leave through an outbox after the authoritative commit.

scenarios.label: Catalog listing
scenarios.summary: A listing contains a variable set of attributes and is commonly displayed as one object. Most requests fetch the full listing by its ID or a stable lookup key.
scenarios.result: A document can make the aggregate simple to evolve and fetch. Keep ownership of canonical SKU, price, and inventory facts explicit when they also appear elsewhere.

scenarios.label: Session lookup
scenarios.summary: The application receives a session ID and needs a small bounded record quickly. The record expires and can be recreated from the authoritative account state when needed.
scenarios.result: A key-value store with a TTL is a natural fit. Do not make it the only record of a fact whose loss would alter billing, entitlement, or audit history.

scenarios.label: Fraud ring
scenarios.summary: An investigator asks which accounts share devices, cards, addresses, and recent transactions within several hops. The relationship path is the central query, not a single record lookup.
scenarios.result: A graph model can make multi-hop traversal direct. Keep a source-of-truth and an update pipeline for the relationships so the graph does not become an unexplained second writer.
